question: Where does a re-sync that changes nothing spend its time, and can it skip unchanged subtrees?

nodes.title: Re-measure no-op syncs
nodes.question: Where does a no-op re-sync spend its time once the receiver fixes land?
nodes.measure: real-congress and real-psample no-op, push and pull, against rsync; user and kernel time on each end.
nodes.hypothesis: H21: congress no-op push ran at 0.74x rsync's speed, with 408.8 s of CPU against 18.8 s. MA7's pull deficit came from destination path walks.
nodes.decision: B1: at or ahead of rsync both ways. no verdict. The run's status is 'failed' and it carries no lab verdicts, so this branch rests on the arm-vs-control effects alone. Some cells kept only 8 or 9 of 10 blocks. Even so, the hypothesis that xs-rs still trails rsync on no-op re-syncs is refuted. At the default -j4, xs-rs against rsync was 0.269 (0.235 to 0.309, 10 blocks) on congress push and 0.308 (0.262 to 0.361, 10 blocks) on congress pull. It was 0.231 (0.219 to 0.245, 8 blocks) on psample push. The one weak cell is psample pull at -j4: 0.6 with a 95% interval of 0.213 to 1.689 over 9 blocks, too wide to call, at 45.418 s against 75.716 s. At -j8 xs-rs is clearly ahead in all four cells: 0.249, 0.268, 0.185, and 0.191 (0.147 to 0.249) on psample pull. -j1 is also ahead everywhere it is decided: 0.519, 0.584 and 0.421, with psample pull at 0.82 (0.317 to 2.121), inconclusive. Going from -j1 to -j8 roughly halves time on every cell, so no serial bottleneck dominates. xs-rs CPU seconds are close to rsync's at -j4 (7.747 vs 8.098 on congress push), not far above. The lab records only total CPU, not a user/kernel split, so branches 0 and 1 could not be told apart anyway, and neither is needed: xs-rs is at or ahead of rsync both ways. The remaining oddity is the high variance of psample pull at -j4 (and xs-cpp-j4 there at 2.002, 0.912 to 4.393). That is noise worth watching, not a deficit against rsync. A measurement changes no code, so keep is false.

nodes.title: Confirm dest-anchors
nodes.question: Do retained parent descriptors, and single-call opens on Linux, close the gap?
nodes.measure: T17's MA8 (a psample pull onto the Mac, no-op and 1% update) and LC12 (Linux local copies), then openat2 on Linux receivers.
nodes.hypothesis: By hand, the same no-op pull took 29.3 and 36.6 s with dest-anchors, against its parent's 50.5 and 64.0 s and rsync's 50.0 and 51.6 s.
Adopt what helped; the rest of the gap is B3's to close.

nodes.title: Persistent index
nodes.question: Can a no-op skip unchanged subtrees without visiting them?
nodes.measure: Prototype a per-directory hash tree keyed by inode, mtime, ctime and size on both ends, compared root first; later FSEvents and zfs diff. No-op time in milliseconds.
nodes.hypothesis: Most real re-syncs change nothing, yet every name is listed and compared on both ends.
Build it behind a feature bit.

edges.label: at or ahead of rsync both ways
upkeep costs more than it saves
